title: OLM: past, current and future
speaker: OLM A — context and installation; name to confirm
bullets: Past: OLMv0, flawed namespace-local CRD visibility assumptions, SQLite, FBC
caption: Planned: helm+v2 and v2 schemas. Future: OCI catalog storage.
notes: Enumerate the timeline: past work includes OLMv0, SQLite catalogs and established file-based catalogs (FBC). Summarize OLMv0's flawed assumptions about namespace-local CRD visibility, independently managed APIs and watch-aware dependencies. CRD definitions are cluster-scoped shared APIs; custom resource instances may be namespaced, and controller watch scope is configured separately. Shared CRDs can couple operator upgrades. The flawed assumptions belonged to OLMv0's lifecycle model; Kubernetes' cluster-scoped CRD design is the underlying API boundary. Keep the OperatorGroup recap brief and explain how these lessons informed OLMv1. Current OLMv1 capabilities include ClusterExtension, version pins and webhooks. Ongoing development includes resource rollouts, user configuration, direct bundle installation and migration. Direct installation remains an open proposal in PR #2907 at the supplied 2026-10-09 check. Planned work includes Helm content using helm+v2 and v2 catalog schemas. OCI-native catalog storage and transport remain future work. Release-specific availability and feature gates require the source-version qualifications on the detailed slides. The 2025 deck already listed delivered features. A continues with installation changes. Sources: ../kubecon-2025-slide-context.md slide 9; ../kubecon-2026-resource-assessment.md K-1/K-2/V0-2/V0-3; supplied feature-planning context.

title: Streamlined Installation
bullets: The controller uses its own service account.
Restrict ClusterExtension access with RBAC and admission policy.
speaker: OLM A — context and installation; name to confirm
notes: As of operator-controller v1.11.0, the standard installation channel no longer requires spec.serviceAccount. The controller uses its own service account; the deprecated field is ignored. ClusterExtension write access is a high-privilege operation because the controller uses cluster-admin permissions. When delegating access, combine Kubernetes RBAC with appropriate admission policy, such as ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, to constrain allowed extensions. Source: https://github.com/operator-framework/operator-controller/pull/2770 and the v1.11.0 release notes.

title: Namespace Management
lead:
Experimental channel since v1.12.0
Controlled by feature gate
bullets: Set spec.namespace: use an existing user-managed namespace.
Omit it: OLM manages a derived namespace.
Deletion removes that namespace and its contents.
speaker: OLM A — context and installation; name to confirm
notes: Operator-controller v1.12.0 introduced optional spec.namespace in the experimental installation channel. With the feature-gated runtime, an explicitly supplied namespace remains user-managed. When the field is omitted, OLM derives and manages an install namespace using bundle metadata and defaults. Deleting the extension also deletes its managed namespace and all remaining objects in that namespace, including objects OLM did not install. Explain namespace-transition validation and verify the selected bundle and controller version before demonstrating. Sources: https://github.com/operator-framework/operator-controller/pull/2925, https://github.com/operator-framework/operator-controller/pull/2926, https://github.com/operator-framework/operator-controller/pull/2929.

title: Inspect phased resource rollouts
speaker: OLM B — lifecycle primitives and migration; name to confirm
status: IN ACTIVE DEVELOPMENT / CONTROLLED BY FEATURE-GATE
lead: Ordered phases expose resource application and readiness progress.
bullets: Apply resource groups in phase order
caption: Readiness checks show which phase is waiting.
notes: Explain the ClusterExtension → ClusterObjectDeployment → ClusterObjectSet ownership model. ClusterObjectDeployment manages rollout and revision history; ClusterObjectSets hold immutable revisions with ordered phases. observedPhases and other status details help identify stalled objects. Objects within a phase have no defined ordering. The API and rollout behavior are in active development and controlled by feature-gate. Standalone ClusterObjectDeployment use is in active development. A namespace-scoped ObjectDeployment is under consideration, with no committed availability. Sources: https://github.com/operator-framework/operator-controller/pull/3058 and https://github.com/operator-framework/operator-controller/pull/3072.

title: User control of extension deployments
speaker: OLM B — lifecycle primitives and migration; name to confirm
status: IN ACTIVE DEVELOPMENT / CONTROLLED BY FEATURE-GATE
caption: OLM applies user choices through operator configuration.
notes: Describe the deployment as a configuration exchange between users and the operator team. Users express environment, resource, placement, volume and metadata requirements through the package's configuration interface. Operator authors define schema and validation behavior. OLM carries the selected configuration into the deployment. DeploymentConfig is in active development and controlled by feature-gate; values are expressed through ClusterExtension configuration. Explain field-specific merge, replace and append behavior and annotation precedence. Validate example input and inspect the resulting deployment against the pinned source version. Watch-namespace pass-through leaves CRDs shared and supplies no watch-aware dependency management. Sources: supplied customization draft; ../kubecon-2026-resource-assessment.md; ../kubecon-2025-slide-context.md slide 14.

title: OLMv0 → OLMv1 migration
speaker: OLM B — lifecycle primitives and migration; name to confirm
lead: Move operator management from OLMv0 to OLMv1.
bullets: Prepare v1 catalogs from v0 CatalogSources
caption: Structured output supports automation and models.
notes:
Prepare OLMv1 ClusterCatalogs from the existing OLMv0 CatalogSources first. Then evaluate each operator installation for eligibility and preview its migration before transferring management. The check and preview actions evaluate operators; catalog preparation is the earlier prerequisite. The migration specification describes check, convert, rollback and cleanup with ClusterObjectSets. Functionality is supplied as library-olm. The example binaries illustrate library use. The example binaries produce structured output for automation and model consumers. The companion migration scenario exercises JSON Lines output. Eligibility checks have defined coverage. Retaining the namespace can reduce disruption; namespace changes may restart workloads or cause downtime. Validate recovery boundaries and source/gate versions for the selected case. This area is in active development. Sources: library-olm README/spec; ../kubecon-2026-resource-assessment.md; user migration guidance.

Note: Ask Todd to make a separate repo for the binaries (naming is hard :))

title: Install a bundle directly
speaker: OLM B — lifecycle primitives and migration; name to confirm
status: IN ACTIVE DEVELOPMENT / CONTROLLED BY FEATURE-GATE
lead: Select a registry+v1 bundle by its OCI image reference.
caption: Proposed in open PR #2907; controlled by BoxcutterRuntime.
notes: PR #2907 is OPEN and unmerged as of the 2026-10-28 check. Present direct bundle installation as proposed behavior in active development. It supports registry+v1 bundles only and is controlled by the BoxcutterRuntime feature gate. The requested source uses sourceType: OCIImage and source.ociImage.ref. It bypasses catalog resolution. Describe CRD checks and other lifecycle safeguards according to the proposal's supported path; catalog bypass alone establishes no blanket removal of CRD safety. Pin the source revision and gate configuration before preparing an example. The session uses prepared examples without a live demo.

title: Planned Helm content support
speaker: OLM C — content, catalogs and contributions; name to confirm
lead: The rendering contract targets deterministic chart behavior.
bullets: Chart and values produce managed manifests
caption: Standard chart artifacts use a defined rendering contract.
notes:
helm+v2 is the user-confirmed canonical discriminator for versioned OLM Helm packaging/catalog content. Standard chart OCI identity is used, with rendered manifests managed through OLM lifecycle behavior. User values are parsed and validated during rendering. Deterministic rendering is the design goal: features are allow-listed to exclude non-deterministic functionality, with compatibility fixtures required to validate the supported subset. Dependencies are vendored. Hooks and keep behavior are unsupported in the proposal. CRDs use templates/; crds/ is unsupported. Chart release-object mappings and restricted template functions require compatibility testing. Moving CRDs affects upgrade, deletion and data handling. Implementation of proposed gates remains independently unconfirmed. Native chart OCI identity and future OCI catalog storage are separate scopes. Sources: supplied Helm planning brief and feature-planning context.

Transition: the direct-image source motivates future chart content support. The companion Helm experiment uses an OCI image config; standard Helm OCI config handling remains unverified.

title: Catalog performance and content types
speaker: OLM C — content, catalogs and contributions; name to confirm
lead: Design for lower catalog-processing cost and additional content types.
bullets: Direct version fields reduce property traversal
caption: File-based catalogs remain the established foundation.
notes: Credit established FBC capabilities: plaintext editing, composition, extensibility, package-level metadata and version/release properties already exist. The v2 work refines the representation and consumers: less duplicated CSV metadata, version/release fields available directly rather than via property traversal, and explicit mediaType dispatch for installable formats including Helm. Arbitrary FBC schema extensibility alone does not supply end-to-end installation support for a new content type. Catalog processing efficiency is a design benefit to validate, with no measured speedup claimed. Show the practical resolution/metadata work the new representation is intended to reduce. The user-confirmed near-term focus is flexible OLMv1 schemas; OCI-native catalog storage, transport and selective fetching are future work. Channels and legacy graphs are excluded from v2; lifecycle/constraint metadata remains open. Sources: https://olm.operatorframework.io/docs/reference/file-based-catalogs/ ; supplied v2 catalog brief; feature-planning context.
